clue.text: Dictator's time in power reportedly drops form of control

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase before it

blocks.note: a ruler's period in power is a reign

explanation.surface: A dictator's rule, it is said, gives up some way of keeping order.
explanation.walkthrough: REIGN and REIN sound identical; 'drops' merely joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rein is the strap a rider uses to guide a horse, hence any means of restraint or check.

clue.text: Meet again about detaining prisoner in flat

indicators.note: detaining means holding someone in custody, so one word keeps the other locked inside it
in places the word for prisoner inside the word for flat

blocks.note: flat ground is level or even

explanation.surface: A council reconvenes to discuss holding a prisoner in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested containers: the prisoner goes inside flat, and the result goes inside the two-letter word for about.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to assemble once more after a break, a meeting resumed.

clue.text: Football team stopped by for one or two?

indicators.note: a team stopped by something has that thing blocking its middle, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, for one

explanation.surface: A football side is held up by somebody, with the question of whether one or two goals result.
explanation.walkthrough: Inter Milan is the Italian football club. 'one' does double duty, ending the wordplay and starting the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: One and two are whole numbers, examples of integers, hence the question mark marking a definition by example.

clue.text: Opening screen secures name

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the screening word holds the name letter inside it

blocks.note: to vet is to screen or check

explanation.surface: A screen at the start of something fastens a name in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent is a hole or aperture letting air or gas through, an opening.

clue.text: Discharge from canal found in river and mouth of estuary

indicators.note: something found in a place lies within it, so the waterway word sits inside the others
the mouth of a river is where it starts its exit, read here as the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: the Exe, a river in Devon
a cut is an artificial waterway

explanation.surface: Water is let out of a canal where it meets a river near the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A cut is the British term for a canal; the Exe is a Devon river.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge duties is to carry them out or perform them, which is to execute them.

clue.text: Bikini Atoll tests gained notoriety after initially going wrong

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of each of the words before it
letters going wrong fall out of their proper order and must be rearranged

blocks.note: first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Nuclear tests at Bikini Atoll became infamous after early failures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bikini' looks like part of the place name Bikini Atoll, but it is the definition: the following five words supply the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanga is a brief style of bikini or briefs with a narrow side strap.

clue.text: Accountant helping to check correct authorisation

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back by surrounding it, so one word restrains the other inside it

blocks.note: acc. is an abbreviation for account or accountant
a helping or portion is a ration
to edit text is to correct it

explanation.surface: An accountant helps to verify that proper permission has been given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Accreditation is official recognition or approval that someone is qualified, an authorisation.

clue.text: High-tech concession disliked restricting one's time in charge

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the word for disliked keeps the following pieces penned inside it

blocks.note: a sop is a small concession offered to placate
one is I, so one's is I'S
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An unpopular concession limits how long someone can stay in office.
explanation.walkthrough: i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge; the apostrophe s of one's is kept as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophisticated machinery is advanced and complex, which is what high-tech describes.

clue.text: Common feature of publicity explicitly solicited within the law

indicators.note: a feature common to several words is a run of letters they all share, so look inside them

blocks.note: the same five letters sit inside each of these three words

explanation.surface: Publicity that was openly sought is described as legitimate.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual hidden: the answer appears in all three words, not across a word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit means lawful or permitted, the opposite of illicit.

clue.text: Passion seen in counter-revolution

indicators.note: something seen in a word is visible among its letters
counter means running against, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: letters two to five of this word

explanation.surface: Passion is evident in a movement to overturn a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is intense affection or desire, a passion for someone or something.

clue.text: Writing material put back in cupboard and bound together

indicators.note: put back means returned the way it came, so the word runs backwards
in places the writing word inside the cupboard word

explanation.surface: Stationery is returned to a cupboard and tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in the answer falls between the parts of cupboard, not where the pieces join.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-knit group is tightly united, its members bound together by shared ties.

clue.text: Article with literary strength and moral quality

blocks.note: w is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A written piece shows literary power and moral worth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition covers both senses the dictionary gives: muscular strength, and in older use mental or moral qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: Thew is an archaic, literary word for muscle or bodily power, and formerly also for good mental or moral qualities.

clue.text: Anger reflected by very wearing bad mood

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round

blocks.note: dressed in something is wearing it

explanation.surface: Someone's anger shows in being visibly in a foul temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar is used figuratively for sourness or peevishness of temper, an acid ill humour.

clue.text: Cost of transport spoils date

blocks.note: a haul is the booty or spoils taken
a date or period of history is an age

explanation.surface: The price of travelling ruins a romantic evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' and 'date' read as verb and object; both are nouns here.
explanation.definitionFit: Haulage is the charge made for carrying goods by road, a transport fee.

clue.text: New flare-up involving clubs in offensive incident on playing field

indicators.note: involving means including within, so the card suit letter goes inside
in an across clue, A on B puts A after B, so the playing field word comes first

blocks.note: rec is short for recreation ground

explanation.surface: A fresh outbreak of trouble on the pitch involves a nasty clash over golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec is the British short form for a recreation ground, a public playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: Recrudescence is the breaking out again of a disease or trouble after a dormant spell.

clue.text: Intimate papers stolen by Tory supporter close to government

indicators.note: something stolen by a person ends up in their possession, so it goes inside their word
close to means the final letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Private documents are taken by a Conservative activist with links to ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' looks like a verb or adjective, but it is the noun for a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an intimate is a close friend in whom one confides, which is a confidant.

clue.text: Women's boat crew taking up another sport

explanation.surface: A women's rowing team takes up a different sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's rowing is one sport, so 'another sport' is the one in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Weightlifting is a competitive athletic discipline of raising barbells, a different sport from rowing.

clue.text: Gang member in musical based on Romeo

blocks.note: the 1971 stage musical and later film
R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A street gang member appears in a musical adapted from Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests West Side Story; in a down clue, 'based on' puts GREASE above R.
explanation.definitionFit: A greaser is a slang name for a member of a long-haired, leather-jacketed youth gang.

clue.text: Rent trouble's spiralling problem for housing?

blocks.note: rent as past tense of rend, torn
ado is fuss or trouble; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Escalating rents are a problem for the housing market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid for a home, but it is the past participle of rend, ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a spinning column of wind that can destroy houses, a whirling hazard to homes.

clue.text: Flag up string of characters in global search

indicators.note: a string of characters is a run of letters taken from the phrase that follows
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Flag up a sequence of characters while searching the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag up' looks like a phrasal verb, but the definition is the noun Flag alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag, or flagstone, is a flat paving stone, a slab.

clue.text: Divorced legend's despicable character

blocks.note: split the word legend into two words and read it as the end of the leg

explanation.surface: A famous person, now divorced, is a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divorced' tells you to separate legend into LEG END; the heel is at the end of the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The heel is the back part of the foot at the bottom of the leg, and heel is slang for a scoundrel.

clue.text: Spectacular gesture's most generous

indicators.note: the apostrophe s marks what the phrase possesses, its letters

explanation.surface: A grand gesture is the most bountiful one.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no hiding indicator beyond the possessive: the phrase owns the answer among its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Large can mean generous or liberal, as in large-hearted, so the superlative is most generous.

clue.text: Speech ignoring case for proportionate measure

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell of letters, and ignoring it leaves those off

explanation.surface: A speech that neglects the legal case argues for a proportionate response.
explanation.walkthrough: ORATION loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the relation in quantity between two amounts, expressing their proportion.

clue.text: Travel company in outskirts of Barnet for Londoners

indicators.note: Cockney Londoners famously drop the aitch at the start of a word

blocks.note: barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), and its outer edge is the hairline

explanation.surface: An airline company operates on the edge of Barnet, a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is also a London borough, which the surface exploits; the H is lost the way a Cockney speaker says it.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is a company running scheduled flights, a business that transports passengers.

clue.text: British novel that's about English rock

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A British novel concerns English rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath stone is a honey-coloured limestone quarried near Bath, in Somerset, used for the city's Georgian buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath stone is a type of oolitic limestone used in building, so it is a kind of rock.

clue.text: Benefit from Virginia getting into trouble

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the state abbreviation goes inside the other word

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone profits after Virginia gets into difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or advantage, as in to no avail, so it is benefit.

clue.text: Heard substantial chunk of Time is owned by US?

indicators.note: heard means we go by the spoken sound rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a good stretch of time is several hours

explanation.surface: A substantial section of Time magazine is apparently American-owned.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals of Time and US are misleading: the magazine and the country are just time and us. The H of HOURS is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ours is the possessive pronoun for what belongs to us, whatever is owned by us.

clue.text: Missing pair of sale items finally returned

indicators.note: a pair is two, so only two letters of the word are involved
returned means turned back, and finally restricts it to the end of the word

blocks.note: items at an auction are lots

explanation.surface: Two items from a sale went missing and were eventually brought back.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost means gone astray and not found, which is what missing describes.
